chapter: Harlem, Redman's band and the Savoy
title: The Savoy Ballroom's early years: Fess Williams and Chick Webb
summary: Fess Williams opened the Savoy in 1926; Chick Webb's eight-piece band followed with Hodges, Cootie Williams and Truehart.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: -- he was a band from Chicago. He opened the Savoy Ballroom in 1926.
Yes, he did, Fess Williams. He opened the Savoy Ballroom.

And then Chick -- Chick Webb was in there, too. Chick Webb had an eight-piece band. He had two saxophones in there. He had Johnny Hodges on alto and Elmer Williams on tenor, and he had Cootie Williams on trumpet. I don't know who the bass player was.
Was it Elmer James? Maybe Elmer James?
No, no, this is before Elmer's time.
Yeah. I remember when Elmer James was there. But I know the horns, you see. And Jimmy Harrison was on trombone with him for a while.
That's who Chick had for the four horns. And then, of course, the rhythm, he had Bobby Johnson on the guitar. He always did have him. No, Truehart. He had Truehart.
Excuse me. Yeah, Truehart on guitar. But I don't know who the bass was at that time. And then
